conventions.convention: Coefficients are indexed from the oldest value j=0 to the new value j=k, with α_k nonzero; ρ(ζ)=Σα_jζ^j and σ(ζ)=Σβ_jζ^j. The local residual is unscaled, so order p means residual O(h^(p+1)).

The root condition permits repeated roots strictly inside the unit disk, but requires every unit-modulus root to be simple. Zero-stability bounds every homogeneous solution uniformly in the grid length by its starting values.
Variable-step indexing is h_n=t_(n+1)-t_n and r_n=h_n/h_(n-1). The BDF2 residual includes the factor h_n(1+r_n) on the endpoint derivative.
PECE performs exactly one correction using the predicted endpoint derivative, then stores the derivative at the corrected endpoint; it does not solve the implicit corrector equation.

Implicit convergence estimates assume uniform local root existence and uniqueness for every sufficiently close history, and selection of that same root. Variable-step second-order convergence additionally assumes a positive lower ratio bound and an upper ratio bound strictly below 1+√2.

load_bearing.statement: Consistency is order at least one; equivalently ρ(1)=0 and ρ′(1)=σ(1). The root condition requires all roots of ρ to have modulus at most one and all unit-modulus roots to have algebraic multiplicity one.

For the row-shift companion matrix C of ρ/α_k, sup over n≥0 of ||C^n||∞ is finite if and only if ρ satisfies the root condition. Consequently the homogeneous recurrence is zero-stable exactly under that root condition.
For every integer p≥1, the method has order at least p if and only if μ_m=0 for each m=0,…,p, where μ_0=Σα_j and μ_m=Σα_j j^m−mΣβ_j j^(m−1).

Quadratic interpolation gives the BDF2 coefficients (1+2r_n), −(1+r_n)^2, r_n^2 and derivative denominator h_n(1+r_n). For an exact vector solution with bounded third derivative, its unscaled residual is O(h_n^3) uniformly when r_n stays in a fixed compact subinterval of (0,∞).
For homogeneous variable-step BDF2, Δ_(n+1)=q(r_n)Δ_n with q(r)=r²/(1+2r). For r>0, q(r)≤1 exactly when r≤1+√2; an upper ratio bound r_*<1+√2 gives a uniform contraction q_*<1.
The predictor weights are integrals over [t_n,t_(n+1)] of the Lagrange bases on the k known derivative nodes; the corrector weights integrate the bases on those nodes together with the new endpoint.

seams_checked.note: Checked both page contexts and the batch-36 dependency record. This is a retained page prerequisite; no assigned item imports a stationary-iteration proposition or convergence premise.

The absolute-stability definition preserves ρ−zσ, the nonzero leading-coefficient requirement, and the unit-root simplicity condition. The BDF2 root-locus lemma correctly specializes the branch equation to r_n=1.

The constant-step corollary explicitly derives the uniform local selected-root hypothesis before applying the variable-step theorem with r_min=r_*=1. The composed stepper distinguishes exact selected roots from finite residual solves and carries the starter, tube, smoothness, and ratio caveats.
